kings1.20.p1.b1.text: Now Ben-hadad king of Aram assembled his entire army. Accompanied by thirty-two kings with their horses and chariots, he marched up, besieged Samaria, and waged war against it.

kings1.20.p1.b2.text: “This is what Ben-hadad says: ‘Your silver and gold are mine, and your best wives and children are mine!’”

kings1.20.p1.b3.text: “Just as you say, my lord the king: I am yours, along with all that I have.”

kings1.20.p2.b1.text: “…about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to search your palace and the houses of your servants. They will seize and carry away all that is precious to you.”

kings1.20.p2.b2.text: “Do not listen to him or consent to his terms.”

kings1.20.p2.b3.text: “May the gods deal with me, and ever so severely, if enough dust remains of Samaria for each of my men to have a handful.”

kings1.20.p2.b4.text: “Tell him: ‘The one putting on his armor should not boast like one taking it off.’”

kings1.20.p3.b2.text: “This is what the LORD says: ‘Do you see this entire great army? Behold, I will deliver it into your hand this very day, and you will know that I am the LORD.’”

kings1.20.p3.b4.text: “This is what the LORD says: ‘By the young officers of the district governors.’”

kings1.20.p3.b5.text: So Ahab assembled the young officers of the district governors, and there were 232 men.

kings1.20.p4.b2.text: while Ben-hadad and the 32 kings allied with him were in their tents getting drunk.

kings1.20.p4.b3.text: “If they have marched out in peace… take them alive. Even if they have marched out for war, take them alive.”

kings1.20.p4.b4.text: So the Arameans fled, with the Israelites in pursuit. But Ben-hadad king of Aram escaped on horseback with the cavalry.

kings1.20.p5.b1.text: “Go and strengthen your position, and take note what you must do, for in the spring the king of Aram will come up against you.”

kings1.20.p5.b2.text: “Their gods are gods of the hills. That is why they prevailed over us. Instead, we should fight them on the plains; surely then we will prevail.”

kings1.20.p5.b3.text: …horse for horse and chariot for chariot…

kings1.20.p5.b4.text: The Israelites also mobilized… camped before them like two small flocks of goats, while the Arameans covered the countryside.

kings1.20.p6.b1.text: “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because the Arameans think the LORD is a god of the hills and not of the valleys, I will deliver all this great army into your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’”

kings1.20.p6.b2.text: For seven days the armies camped opposite each other, and on the seventh day the battle ensued,

kings1.20.p6.b3.text: The rest of them fled into the city of Aphek, where the wall fell…

kings1.20.p6.b4.text: Ben-hadad also fled to the city and hid in an inner room.

kings1.20.p7.b1.text: “Look now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful… Perhaps he will spare your life.”

kings1.20.p7.b2.text: “Your servant Ben-hadad says, ‘Please spare my life.’”

kings1.20.p7.b3.text: “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”

kings1.20.p8.b1.text: Meanwhile, by the word of the LORD, one of the sons of the prophets… went and waited on the road for the king, disguising himself with a bandage over his eyes.

kings1.20.p8.b2.text: “Guard this man! If he goes missing for any reason, your life will be exchanged for his life… But while your servant was busy here and there, the man disappeared.”

kings1.20.p8.b3.text: “So shall your judgment be; you have pronounced it on yourself.”

kings1.20.p8.b4.text: “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because you have let slip from your hand the man I had devoted to destruction, your life will be exchanged for his life, and your people for his people.’”

kings1.20.p8.b5.text: Sullen and angry, the king of Israel went home to Samaria.
